MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 14, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on March 14, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 9, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Property: 26836 Oso Parkway, Mission
  Viejo Agency Negotiators; Dennis Wilberg, William Curley, and Elaine Lister:
  Negotiating Party: Jamboree Housing Under Negotiations Terms for Previously
  Approved Refinancing.

City Council Minutes  1  March 14, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:00 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council considered one closed session item
regarding real property. The Council provided direction to staff but no reportable action occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Ramona Acosta Recipient of the "May Russell Lifetime Achievement
  Award"

  Mayor Bucknum and representatives for Senator Pat Bates, Congresswoman Mimi
  Walters, and Assemblyman Bill Brough presented certificates of recognition.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following asked Mayor Bucknum to disclose what was discussed in her recent meeting with
Congresswoman Mimi Walters: Deborah Cunningham-Skurnik, M.V.; Jessica Riegert, M.V.;
Vivian Frerichs, M.V.; Jason Guthridge, M.V.; Barbara Scheinman, M.V.; Judith Fike, M.V.; and
Andrea Rangro, M.V.

Kelley Crawford, M.V.: stated that she is an instructor at Montanoso Recreation Center and she
requested the Council's help to replace or repair the sound system in the aerobics room.

Robert D. Breton, M.V.: thanked the City Council Members for ushering Mission Viejo into a new
era. He said that current City projects resonate with every heart, age, sector and segment of the
community and it is clear that the Council Members respect each other’s opinions and wish to end
the divisiveness of the past. As a token of his thanks, he presented the Council Members with a
coffee mug adorned with the original city motto "It's Nice to Have Mission Viejo Around the
House."

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that through a public records request, she received copy of a
questionnaire that indicates the City Council will undertake intensified development at the
shopping center across from city hall.

City Council Minutes  2  March 14, 2017
 Annie Nelson, M.V.: announced that she invited Wendy Bucknum to attend a recent meeting that
she requested with Congresswoman Mimi Walters on behalf of her organization, American Soldier
Network. Ms. Nelson disclosed that the meeting was to seek Congresswoman Walters’ support in
order to make movement in Washington D.C. for veteran’s services and was for no other purpose.

Cynthia Cantrelle, Mission Viejo: stated that Planned Parenthood is conducting abortions in
Mission Viejo and there will be a peaceful protest campaign called “40 days to life” on March 25
and April 8. Ms. Cantrelle invited interested residents to join the protest at the corner of Chrisanta
Drive and La Paz Road.

Jodi Barber, Laguna Niguel: announced that last year there were 211 lives lost to drug overdose in
Orange County and 367 the year before that. Drug overdose is the number one cause of accidental
death in the U.S. and is a major epidemic and health crisis. Ms. Barber asked the City to help her
get a free presentation of her documentary, Overtaken, into more Mission Viejo schools.

Rudy Padrol, M.V.: stated that he has been personally touched by addiction and he asked what
programs are in place in Mission Viejo for people who want help.

Rhonda Reardon, M.V.: thanked resident Annie Nelson for bringing the light of truth to her
meeting with Congresswoman Mimi Walters and, on behalf of Senator Pat Bates and
Assemblyman Bill Brough, she thanked City Manager Wilberg and Assistant City Manager Rattay
for their help with Senior Day 2017. She also announced an upcoming Veterans Resource Fair
and Wounded Warrior amputee softball game on Saturday, March 25 from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. at
Saddleback College.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 5 and 10 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs,
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

City Council Minutes  3  March 14, 2017
 2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 28, 2017, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated February 17, 2017 in the Amount of $1,369,391.77

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated February 24, 2017 in the Amount of $612,109.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2017

  Received and filed.

7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2017

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2017

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for January 2017

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  Council Chamber and MVTV Studio Audio Visual & Broadcast Upgrade Project

  This item was continued to the next City Council Meeting.

10.  Cox Communications State Franchise Certificate and P.E.G. Fee

  Council Member Sachs discussed the 2006 State franchising of cable companies in cities
  and counties and noted that the City of Mission Viejo lost control of the cable providers at
  that time. He reminded residents that the administration of Cox is now managed by the
  Public Utilities Commission (PUC) so residents can file issues or complaints with the PUC.

City Council Minutes  4  March 14, 2017
   He said the City can also discuss concerns with Cox so residents should let the Council
  Members know if they have problems.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Raths, to
  introduce Ordinance 17-323 Reauthorizing Ordinance 07-249, as Amended for Currency,
  Pursuant to California Public Utilities Code Section 5870 (5870N) (Division 2.5) and
  Readopting all Previous Findings, Analysis and Legislative History for Ordinance 07-249.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs,
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

11.  Cultural Arts Master Plan

  Director of Library Services Genesis Hansen presented the staff report.

  Richard Stein, Executive Director of Arts O.C., presented an outline of the proposed
  Cultural Arts Master Plan.

  The following asked the City Council to maintain the Outta Bounds contract and continue
  the program at the Potocki Center: Keerthana Sureshkumar, M.V.; Danielle B., Natasha L.
  Tuley P., Samantha A. and Jack W, M.V.; Jennifer Blyn, M.V.: Joey Likar, M.V.; Anita
  and Jacob Armstrong, San Juan Capistrano, Scott Ramirez, Outta Bounds, Rancho Santa
  Margarita; Kira Likar, M.V.; Denise Likar, M.V.; Katie O'Connor, M.V.; Nihar Mehta,
  M.V.; Carrie and Tuley Polito, M.V.; and Jennifer Posey, Coto de Caza.

  The following expressed support for the Cultural Arts Master Plan: Tim Bardwell, Master
  Chorale of Saddleback Valley, M.V.; Sue Crowson, M.V.; Jean Turner, M.V.; Dr. Marillyn
  Brame, M.V.; Linda Harms, M.V.; Judy Bullockus, M.V.; Shannon Ingram, M.V.; and
  Robert D. Breton.

  Written comments in favor of the Cultural Arts Master Plan were received from Anna T.
  Boyce, M.V.; Helen Workun, M.V.; and Art Villalobos, M.V.

  A written comment in favor of the Outta Bounds program was received from Lidia and
  Frank Apodaca, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  approve the Cultural Arts Master Plan.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  March 14, 2017
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs,
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

12.  Slope Repair Along Oso Creek

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1) ratify
  the City Manager's approval of Contract Amendment #2 to WB Management, Inc., DBA
  Bistline Engineering in an amount not to exceed $160,000: and (2) adopt Resolution 17-
  08 amending the 2016-17 Operating Budget by $130,000 for environmental maintenance
  including slope repair along Oso Creek.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs,
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 9:19, Mayor Bucknum declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:30 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

13.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

14.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

15.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update

  Deputy Jason Duran provided information on an incident at the Shops at Mission Viejo
  yesterday when an informant reported seeing a man with a rifle in the parking lot. It turned
  out to be a plumber carrying a toilet snake in a bag, not a firearm. He also reported the
  arrest of a man who pulled a knife on an off-duty Deputy Sheriff.
City Council Minutes  6  March 14, 2017
 16.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2016-17

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the report.

  A written comment was received from resident Cathy Schlicht requesting that the line of
  sight on southbound Muirlands (at Marathon) be corrected as she fears there may be an
  accident.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-09 Amending the FY 2016-17 Budget for Adjustment to Certain Revenue
  Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs,
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his attendance at the City’s Health Fair where he signed up
for a free month of karate classes at Novastar Martial Arts. While on the topic of personal safety,
he shared that last week some of Mission Viejo’s elite swimmers were competing in Indianapolis
and, while leaving for the airport, one young lady realized that she forgot her jacket in the hotel
room. When she returned to retrieve it, a man tried to force himself into the room and assail her
but she screamed and defended herself and was able to escape without injury. Thankfully the
Indianapolis police responded quickly and arrested the man. Council Member Goodell noted that
the incident reminded him to ask the Chief of Police if the Sheriff's department can meet with the
swim team and talk about personal safety measures and it also prompted him to call and get set up
for his karate classes at Novastar. He said that Novastar is also hosting free child safety seminars
in April and he encouraged residents to take advantage of that.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley congratulated Coach Brian Mulligan and the Capistrano Valley High
School basketball team for winning CIF. She outlined her attendance at recent events including
two Little League opening days, Senior Day, and the La Paz Intermediate School Gold Ribbon
City Council Minutes  7  March 14, 2017
 panel. Council Member Kelley noted that the school is up for a Gold Ribbon award (formerly the
California Distinguished School award) with the State of California. She also discussed upcoming
events including the Veterans Resource Fair and Wounded Warrior amputee softball game on
Saturday, March 25 from 11:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and the Orange County Triathlon at Lake Mission
Viejo on June 4, 2017. Those interested can sign up to participate at www.octriseries.com. Council
Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word of the month is integrity and
the character film is The Natural, which will be shown on Sunday, March 19 at 2:00 p.m. in the
Council Chamber. She concluded with a quote from Michael Josephson: "Character is doing the
right thing, even when it costs more than you want to pay" and from the book Horton Hatches the
Egg: "I meant what I said and I said what I meant. An elephant is faithful 100%."

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths asked the City Manager to find out how the Capistrano Valley High School
student who was hit by a shot-put is doing. He discussed the PACE programs in Mission Viejo
and provided an outline of the programs’ successes and energy and dollar savings in the City.
Council Member Raths commended Mayor Bucknum for her comments earlier regarding the
meeting with Congresswoman Walters on the topic of veteran’s issues. He noted that residents are
showing concern with their inability to reach Congresswoman Walters and he thanked Mayor
Bucknum for approaching the issue as she did.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs read a prepared statement regarding abuse and discrimination through a
recent rash of anti-Semitism that is happening in every state and also in Mission Viejo. He reported
on swastikas that were recently etched at one of the City's park, just yards from a school where
children play. He also discussed an incident at Los Alisos Middle School when a music teacher
said "Heil Hitler" as his students ended the song Hava Nagila. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said that the
unsophisticated and ignorant teacher desecrated a song of hope, joy and celebration with a
reminder of the destruction of human beings and this teacher has offended other ethnic groups
previously. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs called upon the leadership of the school district to properly
address the matter and he called for the teacher's resignation.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum announced that she just returned from a trip to Sacramento with the Association
of California Cities and several legislators. She noted that she will prepare a briefing of what
happened and who she met with to share with the Council at the next meeting. Mayor Bucknum
outlined her attendance at recent events including the Economic Coalition's Economic Report
which is a forecast specific to the region. She also noted that she attended a very good meeting
with the State Treasurer in Sacramento and not only heard some interesting news on things that
are happening, but it was also good to find out that the office is interested in working with and
helping Orange County. In closing, Mayor Bucknum announced that one of the trainers at
Montanoso Recreation Center, Jadon Pollard, recently experienced a medical issue and is fighting
for his life. She said that Jadon is part of the City family and he and his family need prayers.
City Council Minutes  8  March 14, 2017
 STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

City Manager Wilberg drew the Council's attention to two memos that he distributed earlier in the
evening: (1) the monthly update on the progress at the Marguerite Aquatics complex, and (2) a
summary and status of the maintenance contracts that will be going out to bid.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:11 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 28, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

_______________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 28, 2017

City Council Minutes  9  March 14, 2017
